selection_basis: Reuse only already downloaded original/official sources for conditional oral and metabolite branches plus an optional exposure-interpretation boundary in EDA -> animal PK -> PKPD -> translation -> prospective human scenarios -> conditional PTA; no new network retrieval or clinical-starting-dose workflow.

selected.title: A comparative evaluation of models to predict human intestinal metabolism from nonclinical data
selected.applicability_trigger: An oral animal-to-human exposure scenario is explicitly requested and absorption/first-pass inputs can be qualified.
selected.knowledge_added: For an oral translation branch, distinguish absorption Fa, intestinal escape Fg, hepatic escape Fh and apparent oral clearance CL/F; identify IV-plus-oral deconvolution assumptions and uncertainty. Rat Fg is only a screening input in this study.
selected.limitations: Original 31-drug CYP-mediated comparison, not a universal oral model winner. Human IV+oral data used in paper are not available for the target drug; do not transfer study estimates. Fraction-bearing formulas require original MathML.
selected.qwen_use: Triggered bounded source-review packet only; preserve source case and applicability conditions.

selected.title: Assessment of the relative in vivo potency of the hydroxylated metabolite of darifenacin in its ability to decrease salivary flow using pooled population pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic data
selected.applicability_trigger: Measured parent/metabolite PK and evidence that the metabolite may contribute to the studied PD endpoint exist.
key_locators: HTML sec10 and disp-formula1 MathML M1 (joint effect concentration)
selected.knowledge_added: Conditional joint parent/active-metabolite PK/PD construction with observed concentrations, delay-model alternatives, potency-identifiability and binding-basis checks.
selected.limitations: Darifenacin-specific human case and salivary-flow endpoint; no potency estimate, formation fraction, or efficacy result may be transferred to another drug. Some PK formation and bioavailability factors were confounded and fixed by source assumptions.
selected.qwen_use: Triggered bounded source-review packet only; preserve source case and applicability conditions.

selected.title: Guideline on strategies to identify and mitigate risks for first-in-human and early clinical trials with investigational medicinal products
selected.applicability_trigger: Explaining that a prospective human exposure scenario does not itself establish first-in-human clinical suitability; do not activate a clinical starting-dose workflow.
key_locators: PDF p10 section 6.4 (PK/TK evidence and dose-response context)
PDF p11 section 7.1 (anticipated human exposure versus observed animal effects and uncertainty)
selected.knowledge_added: Optional boundary for interpreting prospective human exposure scenarios: anticipated human exposure, nonclinical effect/toxicity exposure, and uncertainty require separate evidence. This source adds no current NOAEL/HED/MRSD input requirement.
selected.limitations: Guideline concerns early clinical risk mitigation, while the current workflow only simulates prospective PK/PD scenarios. No target-drug safety package or clinical dose is supplied; this packet excludes starting-dose algorithm sections. Version/date retained without claiming current supersession status.

excluded.reason: Already present in the 77-source registry, with extracted chunks; do not duplicate.
Downloaded HTML verifies only abstract and link, not article body; no full-text chunk packet.
Original TMDD papers are high quality but apply to a conditional saturable biologic/target-mediated branch, not a presently identified gap in the six-stage core workflow.

Official FDA MRSD guidance is high quality, but its NOAEL/HED/starting-dose algorithm would create a new clinical safety workflow not requested for current prospective human PK/PD scenarios; retain as candidate only.

extraction_limitations: EXTA001 and EXTA003 flat text deliberately omits MathML; inspect original for any formula beyond two separately verified short expressions.
PDF page text is extracted, not visual validation of tables/equations.
New sources are conditional evidence candidates, not approved method policy or target-drug data; none creates a mandatory metabolite, oral, or FIH clinical-starting-dose stage.
